Copy (Body Text): At its simplest, Craps is a game about the total of a roll of two standard dice.
Each roll produces a total from 2 through 12, with the 7 being the most common outcome.
Press Roll.
The two dice are added together. Most bets win or lose based on this total.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
The Pass Line is the standard starting bet.
Place a bet on the Pass Line. Do this by tapping the Pass Line (which will increment up the bet by the selected chip amount)
Player Action Required: or by dragging a chip from your chip tray to the Pass Line box.

Copy (Body Text): The first roll of a new round is called the Come Out Roll. A Come Out Roll is trying to establish a Point.
On the Come Out Roll, a 7 or 11 wins the Pass Line immediately.
A 7 on the Come Out Roll wins your Pass Line bet.
Place another Pass Line bet.
There are multiple ways to win on the Come Out Roll.
An 11 also wins the Pass Line on the Come Out Roll.
It is possible to lose your bet on the Come Out Roll.
Place another Pass Line bet.
Roll the dice.
A 2, 3, or 12 on the Come Out Roll loses the Pass Line bet. You rolled a 3, so your wager is lost.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Come Out Roll of 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, or 10 establishes a Point.
Place a bet on the Pass Line.
Roll the dice.
The Point marker moves to 6. The round now continues until either 6 or 7 is rolled.
Your Pass Line bet wins if the Point rolls again before a 7.
Other dice totals do not resolve the Pass Line bet. The Point stays active.
A 9 does not affect this Pass Line bet. The Point is still 6.
Roll again.
You rolled the Point before a 7, so the Pass Line wins.
If a 7 rolls before the Point, the Pass Line loses. This is called a Seven Out.
Place another Pass Line bet and establish a new Point.
Roll the dice.
Roll again.
The 7 arrived before the Point. The Pass Line loses, and a new round begins.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
After a Point is established, you may add an Odds bet behind your Pass Line bet.
Place a bet on the Pass Line.
Roll the dice.
Place an additional chip in the Odds area behind your Pass Line bet.
Player Action Required: Place Odds bet behind Pass Line

Copy (Body Text): Your original Pass Line bet and your Odds bet both depend on the Point.
The Odds bet pays according to the chance of rolling the Point before a 7.
Roll the dice.
The Pass Line and Odds bets both win, but they use different payout rates.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Come bet follows the same rules as the Pass Line, but it begins after the table Point is already active.
Place a Pass Line bet.
Roll the dice.
Place a chip in the Come area.
The next roll acts like a Come Out Roll for this Come bet.
A 7 or 11 wins the Come bet. A 2, 3, or 12 loses it. Any Point number moves the bet to that number.
Roll the dice.
The Come bet moves to 5. It now wins if 5 rolls before 7.
You may place Odds behind a Come bet after it moves to a number.
Notes: Custom check: come bet on 5 has odds > 0

Copy (Body Text): The table Point is still 8, while your Come bet has its own Point of 5.
Roll the dice.
The 5 wins both the Come bet and its Odds. The Pass Line remains active on 8.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Place bet lets you choose a number directly.
Place a bet on 6.
Your Place bet wins whenever 6 rolls before 7.
Other numbers do not affect this bet.
The 9 does not affect your Place bet on 6.
Roll again.
The 6 rolled, so your Place bet wins.
All active Place bets lose when a 7 rolls.
Roll again.
The 7 removes your Place bet.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A working bet is active on the next roll.
Place a bet on 6.
Use the Off control to make the bet inactive.
An Off bet does not win or lose until it is turned back On.
Roll the dice.
The 6 rolled, but the bet was Off, so no payout occurs.
Turn the Place bet back On.
Roll again.
The bet was working, so the 6 pays.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Buy bet also wagers on a number rolling before 7.
Place a Buy bet on 4.
Buy bets use true odds, with a commission charged according to the table rules.
Roll the dice.
The 4 rolled before 7, so the Buy bet wins.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
The Field is a one-roll bet.
The Field wins on 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11, or 12.
The Field loses on 5, 6, 7, or 8.
Place a chip in the Field.
The bet resolves on the next roll.
A 10 wins the Field bet.
Place another Field bet.
Roll the dice.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Hardway bet wins when an even total is rolled as a matching pair.
Hard 6 means rolling 3 and 3.
Place a bet on Hard 6.
Roll the dice.
The total is 6, and both dice match. Hard 6 wins.
Hard 6 loses if 6 appears as 1 and 5 or 2 and 4.
Place another Hard 6 bet.
Roll the dice.
The total is 6, but the dice do not match. Hard 6 loses.
A 7 also removes active Hardway bets.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
Proposition bets predict the result of the next roll.
Each proposition bet wins or loses immediately after one roll.
Place a bet on Any 7.
Roll the dice.
The next roll was 7, so the bet wins.
Proposition bets often offer larger payouts because they win less frequently.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Hop bet predicts the exact dice combination on the next roll.
Place a Hop bet on 3 and 4.
The next roll must show a 3 and a 4 for this bet to win.
Roll now.
The exact combination appeared, so the Hop bet wins.
Hop bets on doubles usually use a different payout because there is only one matching combination.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
Bonus bets track a series of results across several rolls.
Unlike one-roll bets, a Bonus bet may stay active through many rolls.
Place a bet on the highlighted Bonus area.
Each qualifying roll marks progress toward the Bonus.
A 7 usually ends unfinished Bonus bets.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
The Don't Pass bet wagers against the shooter making the Point.
On the Come Out Roll, 2 or 3 wins the Don't Pass bet.
A 7 or 11 loses the Don't Pass bet.
A 12 is a push on most Don't Pass tables. Your bet is returned with no win or loss.
Place a chip on Don't Pass.
Roll the dice.
With a Point established, Don't Pass wins if 7 rolls before the Point.
Roll again.
The 7 arrived before the Point, so the Don't Pass bet wins.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Don't Come bet works like Don't Pass after the table Point is already active.
Place a Don't Pass bet.
Roll the dice.
Place a chip in the Don't Come area.
The next roll acts as a personal Come Out Roll for the Don't Come bet.
Roll the dice.
The Don't Come bet moves behind 5. It wins if 7 rolls before 5.
You may add Odds to a Don't Come bet after it moves to a number.
Player Action Required: Place Odds on Don't Come bet (5)
Notes: Custom check: dc bet on 5 has odds > 0

Copy (Body Text): The table Point is still 8, while your Don't Come bet has its own Point of 5.
Roll the dice.
The 7 rolled before 5, so the Don't Come bet and its Odds win.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
A Lay bet wins when 7 rolls before the selected number.

Step Title: The Opposite of a Buy Bet
Copy (Body Text): Buy bets want the number before 7. Lay bets want 7 before the number.
Place a Lay bet against 4.
This bet wins if 7 rolls before 4.
Roll the dice.
The 7 arrived before 4, so the Lay bet wins.
Press Finish to move to the next lesson.
The complete table contains every betting area introduced during the tutorial.
Pass, Come, Don't Pass, and Don't Come follow the Point system.
Place, Buy, and Lay bets target the individual number boxes.
Field, Proposition, and Hop bets resolve on the next roll.
Hardways and Bonus bets may remain active across several rolls.
You now know how each major section of the table works. Choose the bets you prefer and play at your own pace.
